text.p: Australian Mark Philippoussis capped a 20-ace barrage with four in the third-set tiebreaker to power past Brazilian Roberto Jabali 1-6 6-3 7-6 (7-0) Tuesday in the first round of the $303,000 Infiniti Open.

"I don't want to rely on my serve because I work so hard on other parts of my game," said the third-seeded, 13th-ranked Philippoussis, who won 20 of 85 points with aces. "But obviously it helps to have that big serve, to get some free service games."

In other opening-round matches, sixth-seeded American Jim Courier used breaks in the 11th game of each set to dispatch South African Grant Stafford 7-5 7-5 while Sargis Sargsian of Armenia upset eighth-seeded American Alex O'Brien 6-4 6-3. Two-time former champion and fourth seed Richard Krajicek of the Netherlands beat Marcos Ondruska of South Africa 6-4 6-4.
In night play, top-seeded Goran Ivanisevic was to play South African Neville Godwin following a clash between Andre Agassi and fellow American Justin Gimelstob.

Philippoussis, who took a month-long holiday following a disappointing first-round loss at Wimbledon in June, had trouble rubbing off the rust and won just one game in the opening set against Jabali, a nine-year veteran ranked 271st on the ATP computer.
"I've had a couple weeks off and it's the lack of match play," said Philippoussis.
"I think it's the perfect match I needed. I was in a lot of trouble and it's going to help me a lot for my second match."

Philippoussis, nicknamed "Scud" for his record-setting 143 mph (230 kph) serve, got going midway through the second set. He began to riddle Jabali with serves timed as fast as 136 mph (219 kph) and an arsenal of blazing groundstrokes from both sides to level the match at a set apiece.

The two battled on even terms through the third set, forcing a tiebreaker. Philippoussis, however, dominated in the end, exploding four missiles of 127 (204), 129 (208), 125 (201) and 136 mph (219 kph) to close out the one-hour, 43-minute win.
"It was a good tiebreaker," said Philippoussis. "To get off to a good start was important and I just kept on rolling. I think I had pretty good rhythm on the last serves."
